content.title: About
content.content: Coleslaw dressing is a creamy blend of mayonnaise, sour cream, vinegar, and spices designed to coat finely shredded cabbage, carrots, and other vegetables. It gives the dish a smooth, slightly tangy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coleslaw originated in the United States and became popular in the mid‑19th century.
The dressing often contains mustard, which enhances aroma and helps emulsify the mixture.
There are many variations, from classic creamy to lighter yogurt‑based versions.
Some recipes add apple cider vinegar for extra zest.
Coleslaw is commonly served as a side to barbecue, sandwiches, and fried foods.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: The vegetables in coleslaw, such as cabbage and carrots, are rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Probiotic content (when using yogurt)
items.content: Yogurt‑based dressing contains live cultures that promote gut health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and other phytochemicals help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Unlike many sauces, classic coleslaw dressing does not contain added sugars.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acidity of vinegar stimulates stomach acid production, improving digestion.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The dressing often contains mayonnaise and sour cream, which can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The creamy base makes the dressing calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Raw egg content (in mayonnaise)
items.content: Traditional mayonnaise may contain raw eggs, posing a salmonella risk for vulnerable groups.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Many dressings are salty; those with hypertension should choose low‑salt versions.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Toss the dressing with thinly shredded cabbage, carrots, radish, and onion. Mix well and let it rest for 15–30 minutes for flavors to meld. It can also be used as a sandwich spread, in wraps, or as a dip for vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dressing in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, it is best used within 5–7 days. Discard if you notice off‑smell, color change, or mold.
